title: Sails Condition Algebra 1.0
description: NOT a LeafEvaluator (docs/CORE_IMPLEMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE.md section 11's own 'distinguishability of role, not necessarily of concrete type' — the same reasoning that already gave CorrespondenceEvaluator its own separate role rather than reusing LeafEvaluator). A LeafEvaluator produces a ConditionResult from raw domain facts (e.g. the timelock evaluator, from deadline/evaluationTime); this identity instead COMPOSES already-produced ConditionResult values into an aggregate ConditionResult, per the frozen Condition Algebra (docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 13). It governs the shared composition mechanism any composing Ruleset would rely on — no currently-published Ruleset (including sails-escrow-timelock-expiry-ruleset-1.0, the only Ruleset published as of this identity's registration) actually declares a composite AND/OR/threshold condition; this identity exists to make the underlying mechanism conformance-checkable ahead of the first Ruleset that needs it, exactly as sails-timelock-evaluator-1.0 was registered before any Ruleset consumed it. A TypeScript reference implementation exists at packages/sails-core/src/condition-result.ts (conditionAnd/conditionOr/conditionThreshold), but that implementation is not itself the definition of this identity — docs/CORE_IMPLEMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE.md section 19 (Language Neutrality).

inputs.name: op
inputs.description: Which composition operator this vector exercises. AND and OR take two or more ConditionResult children; THRESHOLD additionally takes an integer n.

inputs.name: n
inputs.description: The threshold count N-of-M. Present only when op = "THRESHOLD"; absent (and not applicable) for AND/OR, which are the N=M and N=1 special cases of the same underlying rule respectively.

inputs.name: args
inputs.description: The already-evaluated child ConditionResult values being composed, in the exact case/order given — order is asserted NOT to affect the result for AND/OR/THRESHOLD (see the permutation-invariance vectors), but is preserved in the vector's own input for auditability.

output.rationale: All four states are genuinely reachable by composition even when individual children are drawn from a narrower evaluator (e.g. the timelock evaluator alone never reaches UNSATISFIABLE or UNKNOWN, but AND-ing its result with a child that can reach those states can).

rule: Total order: UNSATISFIABLE < UNKNOWN < NOT_YET_SATISFIED < SATISFIED (docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 13). AND(args) = min(args) over this order; requires at least one arg, rejects (never silently answers) an empty args array. OR(args) = max(args) over this order; same non-empty requirement. THRESHOLD(n, args): counting s = count(SATISFIED), p = count(NOT_YET_SATISFIED), k = count(UNKNOWN), f = count(UNSATISFIABLE) among args — if s >= n then SATISFIED; else if s+p+k < n then UNSATISFIABLE (target unreachable even optimistically); else if s+p >= n then NOT_YET_SATISFIED (already-known paths alone suffice); else UNKNOWN (reaching n requires at least one uncertain slot to resolve favorably). THRESHOLD(1, args) reduces to OR(args); THRESHOLD(M, args) with M = args.length reduces to AND(args). AND, OR, and THRESHOLD are all order-independent (commutative/grouping-independent) over args, per section 13's own verification note.
determinism: Pure function of (op, n, args) only — no side effects, no hidden inputs, no implicit clock or external state. The same input always produces the same output.
normativeReferences: docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 (Condition Semantics — the four-state definitions)
docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 13 (Condition Algebra — the AND/OR/threshold rule this identity implements verbatim)
docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 14 (UNKNOWN / System-Error Boundary — governs the empty-input rejection: a Runtime assembly failure must never silently become a ConditionResult)
